meta.title: A morning on Pulau Ubin | Five Foot Way Journal
meta.description: The first bumboat from Changi, a rented bicycle, the Chek Jawa boardwalk and nasi lemak on the way home: a morning on Singapore's kampong island.

title: A morning on Pulau Ubin
excerpt: The first boat, a bicycle with one gear too few, and the quietest morning in Singapore.

body.p: The best way to see Pulau Ubin is to be on the first boat. Changi Point Ferry Terminal is a small, open shed beside the hawker centre, and on weekday mornings the passengers are a mix of residents with shopping bags, cyclists, birdwatchers with long lenses and a few visitors. The boat leaves when it has enough people. Nobody seems to mind waiting.

It takes about ten minutes. The bumboat, a wooden motorboat with bench seats and a canopy, crosses a channel busy with ships at anchor, and suddenly the city is behind you. Ahead is a low green island with a jetty, a few roofs and no towers at all.

The village by the jetty has a handful of bicycle shops, a provision store, a few seafood restaurants and a shrine. Rent a bike, check the brakes, and agree what time you will bring it back. The lanes are quiet but hilly in places, and the heat builds quickly once you leave the shade.

At the eastern tip, the Chek Jawa boardwalk runs through mangroves and out over the sea. At low tide the shore below is full of life: crabs, mudskippers, sea stars. From the viewing tower you look over the canopy towards Malaysia. In the early morning you may have it almost to yourself.

In the inter-monsoon months, plan to be back on the mainland by early afternoon. Return the bike, take the boat, and finish where you started: at Changi Village Hawker Centre, with a plate of nasi lemak and a cold lime juice, ten minutes from the airport.

ul: **Bring cash** for the boat and the bike rental.
**Carry water** and sun protection; shade is patchy on the lanes.
**Respect the residents**: the kampong houses are homes, not exhibits.
